evidence: Cic. de Or. 1.11: multō pauciōrēs ōrātōrēs (Lewis & Short)
Caes. BG 1.6: multō facilius atque expedītius iter (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: multō melior, far better; with verbs of preferring, multō mālō, I’d much rather (Cic. Att. 12.21.1, Lewis & Short).
With comparatives longē is poetic and post-Augustan (Lewis & Short); classical prose says multō.

terms.gloss: easily, beyond question (with superlatives, prīmus, prīnceps)
evidence: Cic. Fam. 6.10.2: ōrdinis tuī facile prīnceps
Cic. Rosc. Am. 15: ejus vīcīnitātis facile prīmus
terms.comment: English “easily the best”. Lewis & Short: often in Cicero, rare elsewhere.

phrases.latin: vēnit vīlissima rērum hīc aqua, sed pānis longē pulcherrimus
phrases.english: here water, the cheapest thing there is, is sold for money; but the bread is by far the finest

sources: Lewis & Short: multo · Lewis & Short: longe · Lewis & Short: veneo · Lewis & Short: facilis (facile)
Cicero (Fam. 6.10.2, Rosc. Am. 15) checked against the Perseus Latin texts.

Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-horatius), checked against the editions named there. In Hor. S. 1.5.88 we write vēnit (from vēneō, is sold), as the metre requires; the collection has venit.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 313.
